clue.text: Old-fashioned Spanish gentleman bit the dust

parts.note: passé is French-derived for out of date
Don is the Spanish courtesy title for a gentleman

explanation.surface: An outdated Spanish nobleman has finally died.
explanation.definitionFit: To bite the dust and to pass on are both idioms for dying.

clue.text: Pigtails I incorporated into French dishes

indicators.note: incorporated into means placed within, so the letter goes inside the French word

parts.note: plats is French for dishes

explanation.surface: I worked braids into some French cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Braided lengths of hair hang like tails at the back of the head.

clue.text: Stores given public funds

explanation.surface: Shops handed money from the government.
explanation.definitionFit: Stocks are supplies kept in reserve; government stocks are securities issued for public borrowing.

clue.text: Offer made by former nurse

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
to tend is to nurse or care for

explanation.surface: A proposal from someone who used to be a nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend an invitation or thanks is to offer it.

clue.text: No longer working as a mason

explanation.surface: A retired stonemason, or one who has left the Freemasons.
explanation.walkthrough: A Freemason belongs to a masonic order; the second sense is a pun reading the phrase literally as someone outside that brotherhood.
explanation.definitionFit: A broken machine is not functioning; read literally, someone not in the masonic brotherhood.

clue.text: Continue cheerfully even if shares are down

explanation.surface: Keep smiling, investor, even when the market is falling.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is a pun: a bear is a stock-market trader who expects shares to fall, so a bear could be pleased, 'up', when shares are down.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay brave and cheerful under strain is to keep one's spirits high; a bear profits from a falling market.

clue.text: The army manoeuvre requiring physical exertion

explanation.surface: Military drills that demand plenty of stamina.
explanation.definitionFit: A military exercise is a practice operation; exercise also means bodily activity for fitness.

clue.text: Feel confident about US currency of late

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for trust wraps round the coin

parts.note: to rely on something is to trust it confidently
a cent is a unit of American money

explanation.surface: Lately I have trusted the dollar.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done lately happened not long ago.

clue.text: Every year ladies repaired the fence

parts.note: PA stands for per annum, Latin for each year

indicators.note: repaired means mended or reworked, so the letters of ladies are rebuilt

explanation.surface: Each year the women mended the garden fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repaired' signals the anagram; 'Every year' is the Latin per annum, a convention for PA.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockade of stakes forms a defensive barrier or enclosure.

clue.text: A naval NCO has to declare his desertion

definitions.note: the clue names the person by his act: one who has deserted his faith

parts.note: PO stands for petty officer, a naval non-commissioned officer
to state is to declare

explanation.surface: A petty officer is required to own up to having gone absent without leave.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: it points to the man guilty of deserting a religion or cause rather than to the act itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade who abandons a religious belief or a party is a traitor to it.

clue.text: Place to hide nice new writing implement

indicators.note: something hidden is tucked away inside, so place's abbreviation surrounds the rest

parts.note: PL is a standard abbreviation for place, as in street names

indicators.note: something made new is altered, signalling the letters of nice are rearranged

explanation.surface: Where can I stash my nice new pen or pencil?
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' signals the anagram of NICE, which 'to hide' places within the abbreviation for place.
explanation.definitionFit: Graphite in a wooden case is a common tool for drawing and writing.

clue.text: Withdrawn from sale after a copy was made

explanation.surface: An item pulled from the shop once it had been counterfeited.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods taken off the market are withdrawn; to take someone off is to mimic or imitate them.

clue.text: Cakes once cooked aboard ship

indicators.note: things aboard a vessel sit within it, so the steamship letters enclose the rest

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are prepared in a new way, rearranged

explanation.surface: The galley crew baked some cakes while at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' signals the anagram of ONCE, and 'aboard' puts it within the steamship letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A scone is a small baked teacake, typically served with jam and cream in Britain.

clue.text: Dutch punter gets a small beer

parts.note: a punter places bets, so is a better
a half is half a pint of beer

explanation.surface: A gambler from the Netherlands is given a half pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' is not about the Netherlands: in Cockney slang 'my old Dutch' means one's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are affectionate British terms for a spouse, specifically a wife.

clue.text: Ideal fare for a young man joining ecology party

indicators.note: joining tells us one piece is attached to the next, here the party coming first

parts.note: the Greens are the environmentalist political party
a lad is a youth or boy

explanation.surface: A dish recommended for a lad who signs up with the environmentalists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word; 'young man' and 'ecology party' read as one scene, but they give separate pieces, with 'joining' putting the party first.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl of lettuce and leaves is a healthy, perfect meal in many eyes.

clue.text: Test first devised by a writer

parts.note: to essay is to try or test
1ST, with the figure read as I, is first

explanation.surface: An exam was originally set by an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devised by' is just a link; IST comes from 1ST with the digit 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who composes short prose pieces on a subject is an author of that form.

clue.text: Settle one's differences and compensate for time lost

explanation.surface: Patch up a quarrel and recover the hours you missed.
explanation.definitionFit: Reconciling after a row is to be friends again; recovering lost ground is to make good.

clue.text: A number of words used to pass judgment

explanation.surface: A string of words spoken by a judge in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammatical unit of words is one sense; a judge pronouncing punishment is the other.

clue.text: Bank accounts for country people way back

parts.note: a state is a nation or country
men are people

indicators.note: back tells us the abbreviation for way is read from right to left

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A nation's records of how its rural folk fared in times past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ST (street) into TS. 'country people' looks like rural folk, but it gives two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Banks send periodic printed records of a customer's transactions.

clue.text: Make disclosure about calves' meat

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in letters
veal is meat from young calves

explanation.surface: Tell the truth about where the veal comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncover or divulge something is to make it known.

clue.text: Pieces removed from china tea set without anxiety

indicators.note: pieces taken out of a phrase are runs of its letters, so the answer lies inside these words

explanation.surface: Breakages from a porcelain tea service, oddly calming.
explanation.definitionFit: Relaxed and free from worry, as soldiers standing easy are.

clue.text: Bill needs an outlet in pre-Christmas season

parts.note: an ad is a bill or advertisement
a vent is an outlet for air or steam

explanation.surface: A poster needs a shop to sell from during the festive build-up.
explanation.definitionFit: The church season of four weeks leading up to Christmas.

clue.text: A hearth goddess in Zoroastrian Scriptures

parts.note: Vesta was the Roman goddess of the hearth and home

explanation.surface: A deity of the fireside appears in Persian sacred texts.
explanation.definitionFit: The sacred texts of the ancient Persian Zoroastrian religion are known by this name.

clue.text: Stopped getting taken into custody

explanation.surface: Halted, then hauled off to the police station.
explanation.definitionFit: Growth that is checked is halted; a suspect detained by police has been nicked.

clue.text: The purpose of camping?

explanation.surface: What is the point of sleeping under canvas?
explanation.walkthrough: Split as IN TENT, the second sense is a pun on camping out under canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: An aim or goal is one's purpose; a camper sleeps within canvas shelter.

clue.text: The charge for a club is steep

parts.note: a mace is a heavy club used as a weapon
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: The fee to join a golf club is excessive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steep' looks like an adjective about the price, but it is the verb meaning soak.
explanation.definitionFit: To soak food in liquid until soft is to steep it.

clue.text: Drinker imbibing quietly is a good sort

indicators.note: imbibing means taking something in, so the drinker word swallows the quiet letter

parts.note: a toper is a heavy drinker
P is piano, the musical instruction to play quietly

explanation.surface: A drinker who keeps his voice down is a decent fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: In old British slang a splendid, decent person is a real brick.

clue.text: A female articulate and prosperous

parts.note: an articulate speaker is fluent

explanation.surface: A woman who is both well-spoken and wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone affluent is wealthy and well off.
